$comment: Labelled fixtures for the conformance auditor. Every expectation here was
established by reading the repository, not by running the auditor and
recording its output — a fixture set derived from the tool under test
Each entry records why the expectation holds, so a future change that
breaks one of these has to argue with the evidence rather than just
update the number. The three false-positive classes found in the first

evidence.unpublishable-scope: package.json name is @deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-check but the repository owner is omdsh-dev; only the deepseek-ai npm organisation can publish that scope, and the registry returns 404 for the name
evidence.missing-rewrite-imports: tsconfig.json sets rewriteRelativeImportExtensions: true, so relative .ts imports are rewritten on emit by tsc; this is correct TypeScript 5.7 usage
evidence.stale-ts-imports: the .ts occurrences in lib/*.js are inside doc comments and an extension-name string constant, not import specifiers
evidence.lib-layout-mismatch: tsconfig outDir is lib and main is lib/index.js; the prefixes agree
evidence.types-path-mismatch: declarationDir is lib/types and types is lib/types/index.d.ts; the prefixes agree

fixtures.label: compliant, builds via a separate tsconfig

evidence.no-manifest: package.json exists on the default branch at 2385 bytes; an earlier verdict of no-manifest came from a truncated fetch that extracted 15 of 38 files
evidence.missing-rewrite-imports: src contains no relative .ts import specifiers at all, so the check has nothing to fire on
evidence.missing-peer: peerDependencies declares @deepseek-ai/dsh-settings and @deepseek-ai/schemastery; a client plugin need not peer-depend on cordis under its bare name
evidence.lib-layout-mismatch: build configuration lives in tsconfig.build.json, not tsconfig.json, so reading only tsconfig.json cannot conclude a mismatch

fixtures.label: compliant, esbuild bundle without a lib checkout

evidence.missing-rewrite-imports: src does import relative .ts paths, but build.mjs compiles with esbuild in bundle: true mode, which resolves and inlines imports so no .ts specifier survives into lib/
evidence.missing-main-or-types: main is lib/index.js and lib/ is a build artefact absent from a source checkout; its absence in a fresh clone is expected, not a manifest defect
evidence.no-build-entry: scripts.build is 'node build.mjs', so a build entry exists even though lib/ is not committed

fixtures.label: two tsconfigs with opposite layouts, both in use

evidence.lib-layout-mismatch: scripts.build runs 'tsc -p tsconfig.build.json && node scripts/build-client.mjs && tsc -p tsconfig.json': tsconfig.build.json has outDir lib and emits the JavaScript that main (./lib/index.js) points at, while tsconfig.json has outDir lib/types and emits the declarations that types (./lib/types/index.d.ts) points at. Reading only tsconfig.json compares lib/types against main and reports a mismatch that does not exist
evidence.types-path-mismatch: types is ./lib/types/index.d.ts and tsconfig.json emits there, so the declaration layout agrees

fixtures.$why: Added while trying to lock the tsconfig.build.json candidate list. It does NOT lock it: this repository's tsconfig.json extends ../dsh/tsconfig.base.client.json, a path outside the repository, so in a standalone checkout the extends chain cannot resolve and the layout comparison is skipped before it can misfire. The fixture is kept because it pins tsconfig-extends-unresolved behaviour on a real out-of-tree extends, which is common in this ecosystem.
fixtures.$unverifiedPath: Reading tsconfig.build.json in preference to tsconfig.json remains UNVERIFIED by any fixture. Removing it from the candidate list leaves this suite green. Locking it needs a repository with two tsconfigs, an outDir declared in tsconfig.json, no unresolvable extends, and layouts that disagree; a scan of the top 60 compliant plugins did not find one before timing out. Do not claim this path is tested.

evidence.no-tsconfig: the package ships JavaScript with a committed lib/ and no TypeScript sources; requiring a tsconfig would penalise a valid plain-JS plugin
evidence.no-source-entry: there is no src/ because lib/ is authored directly; absence of src is not a defect for a plain-JS package
evidence.missing-rewrite-imports: no TypeScript sources exist, so extension rewriting is irrelevant
